greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers us into his own Body, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to repentance and new life: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you cultivate the ground of our hearts with your grace: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the head of the Body and the source of our growth: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Let us go rejoicing to the house of the Lord.
homily:
We often think of growth as a straight line. We imagine it as a ladder we are climbing, or a project we are steadily finishing, one step after another, one floor after another. We look at our lives and we measure them by what we have achieved, by the skills we have mastered, or by the milestones we have reached. It is a very human way of seeing things. It feels safe to think that if we just work hard enough, if we just keep our eyes on the horizon, we will arrive at the stature we are meant to be. But the Scriptures today offer us a much deeper, more challenging, and ultimately more comforting vision of what it means to be alive in Christ.

St. Paul, writing to the Ephesians, speaks of 'the full stature of Christ.' He does not describe this as a solo climb. He describes it as a body. He speaks of ligaments and joints, of the proper functioning of each part. He tells us that we are joined and held together. Think of that image: we are not isolated individuals trying to reach the top of a mountain on our own. We are like the individual parts of a great, intricate machine or a living organism. If one part is missing, the whole body feels it. If one part is flourishing, the whole body benefits. We are connected in ways we cannot always see, held together by a love that is stronger than any distance.

Benjamin Vo understood this connection. He was a boy who saw the world as a place of infinite, beautiful complexity. Think of his mind—that brilliant, analytical mind that could dive into the depths of cloud infrastructure and high-level logic. He wasn't just learning how to code; he was learning how systems work, how things are held together, how to build something that could carry information and connection across the globe. He dreamed of 'con chim airlines'—a name that always brought a smile to his face, a giggle that lit up the room. Why? Because it wasn't just about the planes. It was about the joy of movement, the wonder of flight, the desire to connect one place to another. He saw the world as a place meant to be traversed, meant to be shared, meant to be held in common.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has felt like a disruption in the rhythm of that body. You look at the empty chair, you look at the space where Ben’s laughter used to be, and you feel as though a vital part of the structure has been removed. It is a heavy, disorienting experience. You wonder how the body can function when a piece of it is no longer visible to the eye. But Paul reminds us that we are built into him. We are not just held together by our own presence; we are held together by the presence of Christ. The bond you share with Benjamin is not a memory of the past; it is a living, breathing reality in the heart of God. He is not gone from the Body; he is simply in a different part of the house, a part where the view is clearer and the joy is complete. You are a family of four, and that is a truth that exists beyond the reach of time.

There is a temptation, when we are trying to understand our lives, to look for reasons. We want to know why the fig tree in the Gospel did not bear fruit, or why the tower fell at Siloam. We want to solve the equation. We want to know if we missed a sign, or if there was something we should have done differently. I want you to hear this clearly: you missed nothing. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the ones who provided the soil in which his beautiful, gentle spirit could grow. You gave him the love, the curiosity, the encouragement, and the home that shaped him into the person he was. You are not the ones who determine the harvest; that belongs to the Gardener. You are the ones who were called to tend the tree, and you did so with a devotion that is a reflection of the Father’s own heart.

In the Gospel today, Jesus tells a story about a fig tree. The owner wants to cut it down because he sees no fruit. But the gardener—the one who knows the tree, the one who has spent time with it, the one who has invested in it—he asks for more time. 'Sir, leave it for this year also, and I shall cultivate the ground around it and fertilize it.' This is the work of the Lord in our lives. Even when we feel like we are barren, even when we feel like the fruit of our joy has been taken away, he is there. He is the Gardener who is constantly cultivating the ground of our hearts. He is the one who is fertilizing the soil with his grace, preparing us for a growth that we cannot yet see. He is not looking for a quick harvest. He is looking for a deep, enduring life.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the geometry of this love better than anyone. You know the way the house feels, the way the memories are woven into the very fabric of your life together. You are the one who carries the legacy of his curiosity. When you look at the sky, when you think of the planes, when you feel the quiet of the house, know that you are a vital part of this living body. You are the one who knows what it means to be a brother, to be a friend, to be a witness to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who sees the beauty in the small things. You are a witness to the world that love is stronger than any distance, that it is the most beautiful material in the universe.

There is a moment in a dream that your father shared—that beautiful, simple moment of waiting in line for ice cream, where Ben was the one who paid. It is a small thing, a mundane, human thing. But in the landscape of our longing, it is a mountain of hope. It is a sign that the roles we play, the love we share, the simple, everyday gestures of affection—they do not end. They are gathered up. They are held. They are the currency of the Kingdom of Heaven. When you feel the ache of his absence, remember that he is not lost. He is just waiting in a different line, in a place where the ice cream never melts and the sun never sets. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile, the one that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the Gardener’s work has already accomplished its purpose in him.

We are living in a time that often feels like a long, cold autumn. We see the leaves falling, we feel the air turning, and we are tempted to look for security in the things we can control. But Jesus is inviting us to look at the Gardener. He is inviting us to trust that the ground we are standing on is holy. He is not distant. He is the one who is kneeling with you in the silence. He is the one who is holding your hand when the night is at its deepest. He is the one who is whispering to your hearts that you are not alone, that you are not forgotten, and that you are loved beyond all measure.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is not a new set of plans. It is a simple, quiet, doable thing: keep your heart open to the cultivation of the Spirit. When you feel the ache, do not turn away from it. Let it be the place where God meets you. When you see someone who is struggling, when you see someone who is thirsty, when you see someone who is just trying to make it through the day, remember that they, too, bear the image of the Creator. Reach out to them. Give a little of your time, a little of your heart, a little of your kindness. Not because you have to, but because you are overflowing with the love that Benjamin left behind. You are the stewards of his legacy. You are the ones who keep the water moving, just as you have done with the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a sign, a tangible, physical piece of the grace that you are living. It is a sign that the love that was poured into Ben is still flowing, still quenching the thirst of the poor, still bringing life to the dry places. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope, you are adding to that well. You are keeping the water moving. You are ensuring that the legacy of his gentle spirit continues to nourish the earth.

Do not be afraid of the future. The same God who held Benjamin in his hand as he looked out at the sky is the same God who holds you today as you look out at your own horizon. He is not a stranger. He is your Father. He knows the exact shape of your heart, he knows the depth of your longing, and he knows how much you miss the one you love. And he is promising you that the story is not over. The reunion is certain. Keep your eyes on the sky. Keep your heart in the light. And remember that he is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the banquet is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may his face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may he give you his peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ.
For all who carry the heavy cross of grief, that they may be consoled by the promise of the Resurrection and find hope in the presence of God.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Grace was given to each of us
according to the measure of Christ’s gift.
Therefore, it says:He ascended on high and took prisoners captive;
he gave gifts to men.What does “he ascended” mean except that he also descended
into the lower regions of the earth?
The one who descended is also the one who ascended
far above all the heavens,
that he might fill all things.And he gave some as Apostles, others as prophets,
others as evangelists, others as pastors and teachers,
to equip the holy ones for the work of ministry,
for building up the Body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of faith
and knowledge of the Son of God, to mature manhood
to the extent of the full stature of Christ,
so that we may no longer be infants,
tossed by waves and swept along by every wind of teaching
arising from human trickery,
from their cunning in the interests of deceitful scheming.
Rather, living the truth in love,
we should grow in every way into him who is the head, Christ,
from whom the whole Body,
joined and held together by every supporting ligament,
with the proper functioning of each part,
brings about the Body’s growth and builds itself up in love.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1) Let us go rejoicing to the house of the Lord.
I rejoiced because they said to me,
“We will go up to the house of the LORD.”
And now we have set foot
within your gates, O Jerusalem.
R. Let us go rejoicing to the house of the Lord.
Jerusalem, built as a city
with compact unity.
To it the tribes go up,
the tribes of the LORD.
R. Let us go rejoicing to the house of the Lord.
According to the decree for Israel,
to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
In it are set up judgment seats,
seats for the house of David.
R. Let us go rejoicing to the house of the Lord.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Some people told Jesus about the Galileans
whose blood Pilate had mingled with the blood of their sacrifices.
He said to them in reply, 
“Do you think that because these Galileans suffered in this way 
they were greater sinners than all other Galileans?
By no means!
But I tell you, if you do not repent,
you will all perish as they did!
Or those eighteen people who were killed 
when the tower at Siloam fell on them–
do you think they were more guilty 
than everyone else who lived in Jerusalem?
By no means!
But I tell you, if you do not repent,
you will all perish as they did!”And he told them this parable: 
“There once was a person who had a fig tree planted in his orchard, 
and when he came in search of fruit on it but found none,
he said to the gardener,
‘For three years now I have come in search of fruit on this fig tree 
but have found none.
So cut it down.
Why should it exhaust the soil?’
He said to him in reply,
‘Sir, leave it for this year also, 
and I shall cultivate the ground around it and fertilize it; 
it may bear fruit in the future.
If not you can cut it down.’”

day: Saturday of the Twenty-ninth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.
